# ces-revisions roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-27. Background: specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-chatgpt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-claude.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-gemini.md.
Choices made:
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), uv-managed package (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`), pytest and ruff for dev.
- Python/JAX stack as named in specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md: NumPyro, Dynamax, ArviZ, Polars.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | How the size of the one-month revision moves with the number of collection days before first release | A | 1 | Release calendar and monthly vintages: a day or two to assemble; one fit on ~40 years of monthly vintages: measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | How much of the one- and two-month revisions comes from late sample reports, and how much from seasonal-factor revision | A | 2 | Needs NSA and SA vintages together; fit time measured by Stage 1 first |
| O2 | How the size of the two-month revision moves with the first-closing collection rate | A | 3 | Collection-rate series from published CES tables; fit time measured by Stage 1 first |
| O6 | How revision size moves with CES sample size and sample attrition | B | 1 | Several days to hand-build from technical notes and archived releases; fit time measured by Stage 2 |
| O4 | How revision size moves with real BLS appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdowns | B | 2 | Several days to hand-build from budget justifications |
| O5 | How revision size moves with BLS staffing counts | B | 3 | Several days to hand-build from staffing records and budget justifications |

Tracks (ranked A, then B):
A — Collection interval and revision size (research).
B — Budget, staffing and attrition (research). Split from A because A rests on sharp month-to-month calendar variation that public release dates give directly. B's covariates move slowly, trend together and must be hand-built. B's answer does not change A's model.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Collection days and one-month revision size
      Objective: Estimate, on real CES vintages, how one-month revision size moves with collection days before first release.
      Outcomes: O1
      Track: A
      Consumes: nothing (scaffold package only)
      Produces: specs/ces-revisions-stage-1-findings.md; an assembled monthly vintage panel and release calendar on real data
      Exit: O1: the findings file states the estimated effect of collection days on one-month revision size, with its uncertainty, from real monthly vintages; it records the measured time to assemble the data and the wall-clock time of the real fit.
      Leaves out: full validation suite: suggested, see the approval question; vintage manifest: suggested, see the approval question
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Sample size, attrition and revision size
      Objective: Estimate, on real data, how revision size moves with CES sample size and sample attrition.
      Outcomes: O6
      Track: B
      Consumes: Stage 1's monthly vintage panel (revision sizes)

      Exit: O6: the findings file states the estimated effect of sample size and attrition on revision size, with its uncertainty, from real data; it records the measured time to hand-build the series and the wall-clock time of the real fit.
      Leaves out: covariate source traceability: suggested, see the approval question; full validation suite: suggested, see the approval question
      ROUTING: brainstorming

**Message:**

Do you approve this partition (Stage 1 is Track A's core and delivers O1; Stage 2 is Track B's core, delivers O6 and consumes Stage 1's vintage panel), and will you approve with a rank in its track, or decline, each suggested quality: for Track A, a full validation suite, because claims about revision size need checks aimed at dispersion against a constant-variance baseline and in pseudo-real time (outcome: "Evidence that the revision-size model beats a constant-variance baseline on revision dispersion, including in pseudo-real time"), and a vintage manifest, because BLS does not archive every vintage, so the fetched releases must be pinned (outcome: "A record of every release vintage used, with source and fetch date, that rebuilds the panel"); for Track B, covariate source traceability, because the hand-built series are only as credible as their sources (outcome: "Each sample, budget and staffing figure traced to the document and page it came from"), and a full validation suite, because slow, collinear covariates invite overfit (outcome: "Evidence that the Track B covariates improve on a constant-variance baseline out of sample")?
